Definition: akin to σαφής (clear); wise (in a most general application):--wise. Compare G5429.
BiblicalUsage: The wise man in Scripture is rarely the clever one. If any man seemeth to be wise in this world, let him become a fool, that he may be wise; the Father hid these things from the wise and prudent and revealed them unto babes; and James asks who is a wise man, then answers, let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that wisdom is proved by a meek life, not by a sharp tongue. I believe God hides His truth from the proud and shows it to the humble, and the meek life is the proof.
